caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:hc-20
attempts.entry_title: MEC head-direction cells on a rotating arena (Park et al. 2019)
attempts.summary: Head-direction cells kept their firing rates and pairwise temporal coupling through arena rotation, and their directional tuning degraded during rotation as reported, though this depends on the post hoc test chosen. Ensemble decoding and the alternation between room and arena preference held only under readings the paper leaves open and with one session with misaligned tracks, and the link to shock-zone proximity was weaker (mean r -0.07 against -0.141). Preserved internally referenced tuning between cell pairs did not reproduce on the files as deposited, though it holds without the damaged files, nor did its short-lived arena registration. Learning curves, LFP power and analyses of all MEC cells could not be tested, as only the 115 head-direction cells are deposited.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Park, Keeley, Savin, Ranck and Fenton (2019) on CRCNS hc-20, which holds the spike trains of 115 medial entorhinal head-direction cells from 13 rats, recorded in stable, rotating and stable trials of a place avoidance task, with the tracker files of those trials. It compares directional tuning, firing rates, pair correlations, ensemble decoding, momentary directional information and internally referenced tuning across trials and frames. The other MEC cells, the LFP and the training sessions are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Park et al. (2019) from CRCNS hc-20

outcomes.statement: The paper analyses 115 dorsal MEC head-direction cells from 13 rats, among 353 MEC cells forming 556 cell pairs (Table S1), out of 1594 MEC single units recorded.
outcomes.source: Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 1; STAR Methods, Electrophysiology; Table S1
outcomes.quote: We recorded 115 dorsal MEC head-direction cells (Figure S1; Table S1) from 13 rats
outcomes.notes: The dataset holds 115 head-direction cells from 13 rats in 44 sessions, the paper's count. Per rat the counts match Table S1 except R029 (40 against 41) and R523 (2 against 1). Under the paper's head-direction criteria in stable1 (rate below 10 AP/s, Rayleigh and Kuiper tests at p < 0.05) 110 of 115 pass (83 with the Rayleigh n taken as 36 bins). The 353 MEC cells and 556 MEC pairs of Table S1 cannot be counted, as only the head-direction cells are deposited. The 44 sessions give 146 simultaneously recorded head-direction pairs, against 142 in the Results. The two R523 units come from one session recorded on 1 October 2014 and the three 1001R029 units from a session of 1 October 2013 (tracker headers); the TSD headers carry no date or rat, so the files cannot show where the per-rat difference comes from.
deviations: Only the head-direction count could be tested; the two MEC counts need cells the dataset does not hold.

The Rayleigh test of the classification uses the tuning curve's vector with n the number of spikes (STAR Methods, Quantifying Head-direction Signals, Directionality, which converts the tuning curve's Rayleigh vector to a z statistic without naming n); n = 36 bins is shown as a variant. Spike width cannot be applied without waveforms.

outcomes.statement: The head-direction cells have long-duration spikes and a mean firing rate of 1.41 ± 0.20 AP/s.
outcomes.source: STAR Methods, Data Analysis, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: MEC head direction cells were classified as cells with long duration action potentials (avg. width at 30% of the peak voltage 169.79 ± 4.58 ms) and average firing rate below 10 AP/s (avg. 1.41 ± 0.20 AP/s)
outcomes.notes: Mean stable1 rate 1.392 AP/s (SEM 0.207, median 0.668, range 0.019 to 13.768, n = 115); the mean of the three trials is 1.433 AP/s. Both are within 1.41 ± 0.20. Spike width is not tested.
deviations: Spike width is not tested; no waveforms are in the dataset.

outcomes.statement: The 13 recorded rats learned the place avoidance task, with performance improving over trials in the stable (baseline) and the rotating (challenge) conditions and no trial by frame interaction in the rotating condition.
outcomes.source: Figure 1A legend; Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: right: learning curves from the 13 recorded rats in the stable [baseline]

statistics.about: rotating condition, trial by frame interaction

outcomes.notes: The learning curves come from the pretraining and training sessions. The dataset holds only the stable1, rotating and stable2 recording trials of 44 sessions (88 .dat files under data/DAT/SA and 88 under data/DAT/RA, each a recording trial), and no training sessions.

outcomes.statement: Rotation did not change locomotor speed relative to stable1, measured in either frame, but speed was lower in stable2 than in the other conditions.
outcomes.source: Figure 1C, top left, and its legend
outcomes.quote: Effect of rotation on (top left) speed

statistics.test: repeated-measures ANOVA, Greenhouse-Geisser corrected, Tukey-Kramer HSD

outcomes.notes: Over 44 sessions the condition effect is significant in every reading (p from 2.9e-15 to 3.27e-17) and stable2 is lowest (reading a, 10.82 cm/s against 15.3, 14.64 and 15.67 for stable1, room and arena), below each other condition at p < 0.0001. In reading (a) with steps above 100 cm/s dropped, stable1, room and arena do not differ (repeated-measures Tukey p = 0.9097, 0.2654, 0.0658; between-groups 0.9628, 0.5485, 0.2733). Without that filter the room and arena frames differ at p = 0.0481 (0.2739 with the between-groups Tukey test), and in reading (b), 1 s steps, with or without the filter, they differ at p = 0.0058 (0.0768 with the between-groups test). So the outcome holds in reading (a) with the filter under either Tukey test, and in both readings under the between-groups test; with the repeated-measures test it fails in reading (b) and in reading (a) without the filter. The clean variant (39 sessions) gives the reading (a) pattern with room against arena p = 0.1020.
deviations: Assumed, a filter dropping steps faster than 100 cm/s (tracking jumps), which the paper does not state (the notebook first called it a standard choice; it is this attempt's assumption); the outcome rests on it in reading (a) with the repeated-measures Tukey test, and the unfiltered results are shown.

Assumed, the post hoc Tukey test uses the error term of the repeated-measures ANOVA, as the test that follows a repeated-measures ANOVA (STAR Methods, Statistics); the between-groups Tukey test is shown as a variant.
44 sessions, where the paper's degrees of freedom imply about 38; the paper does not say which sessions it used.

outcomes.statement: Power in the MEC local field potential did not differ across conditions.
outcomes.source: Figure 1C, top right, and its legend; Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Despite excellent navigation (Figure 1A), maintained firing rates, and power in the local field potential (LFP)
outcomes.notes: No LFP is in the dataset; the zip holds TSD spike files and tracker files only, and the data descriptor does not mention LFP.

outcomes.statement: Firing rates of the head-direction cells were maintained across stable1, rotating and stable2.
outcomes.source: Figure 1C, bottom left, and its legend
outcomes.quote: Despite excellent navigation (Figure 1A), maintained firing rates
outcomes.notes: Repeated-measures ANOVA on rate over stable1, rotating and stable2, F(1.35, 154.10) = 1.76, p = 0.184 with the Greenhouse-Geisser correction (Mauchly p = 9.4e-17); the paper gives F(1.34, 153.21) = 1.89, p = 0.17. Means 1.392, 1.71 and 1.198 AP/s (rotating - stable1 0.318, stable2 - stable1 -0.194); the rotating mean includes one unit at 40.1 AP/s (1001R523 P9C1). The clean variant gives p = 0.186. On log rates the trials differ (p = 0.00149), a variant the paper does not use.

outcomes.statement: Directional tuning of head-direction cells was strongly degraded during rotation in both frames, more in the arena frame than in the room frame, and returned in stable2 (stable1 = stable2 > rotating room frame > rotating arena frame).
outcomes.source: Figure 1C, bottom right, and its legend; Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: stable1 = stable2 > rotating-room frame > rotating-arena frame (p < 0.01; post hoc using Tukey-Kramer honest significant difference [HSD])
outcomes.notes: Directionality differs across the four conditions, F(2.77, 315.60) = 72.66, p = 8.88e-34 (uncorrected p = 2.23e-36; paper F(3, 342) = 70.36). Means 0.46 (stable1), 0.421 (stable2), 0.344 (room), 0.17 (arena). With the repeated-measures Tukey test, stable1 = stable2 (p = 0.2652), stable1 > room (p < 0.0001), stable2 > room (p = 0.0019), room > arena (p < 0.0001). With the between-groups Tukey test stable2 against room has p = 0.0553, so the outcome rests on the choice; with that test the claim would be partially reproduced. In the clean variant (99 cells) room is below stable1 at p = 0.0407 and not below stable2 (p = 0.4225), while arena stays below all (p < 0.0001); the excluded sessions include the four whose rotating tracks disagree between frames.
deviations: Assumed, the post hoc Tukey test uses the error term of the repeated-measures ANOVA (STAR Methods, Statistics, and the Figure 1 legend, "ANOVAs on data in (C) and (D) ... with repeated-measures, Tukey-Kramer HSD tests"). The paper does not say which error term; each cell is measured in every condition, and the within-cell error is the one the ANOVA it follows uses. The between-groups Tukey-Kramer test, which ignores the pairing, is shown and gives p = 0.0553 for stable2 against room.

outcomes.statement: The change in preferred direction differs across trial pairs (stable1-stable2 = stable1-rotating room frame > stable1-rotating arena frame), and is greater for every trial pair than between the two halves of stable1.
outcomes.source: Figure 1D, left, and its legend; Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: The rotation-induced change in (left) directional preference differs across trial pairs

statistics.about: trial pairs against the two halves of stable1
statistics.test: ANOVA, Dunnett's test against the stable1 halves

outcomes.notes: Both ANOVAs are significant, three trial pairs F(2.00, 228.00) = 17.80, p = 6.56e-08, and the four groups with the halves F(3, 456) = 19.62, p = 5.55e-12. Every trial pair exceeds the stable1 halves by Dunnett's test (two-sided p = 0.019, 0.0073, < 0.0001; mean changes 58.1, 60.3 and 91.3 degrees against 39.5). The Tukey order is stable1-stable2 = stable1-room (p = 0.9351) < stable1-arena (p < 0.0001), where the legend reads stable1-stable2 = stable1-room > stable1-arena. The between-groups Tukey test gives the same order (p = 0.949, < 0.0001, < 0.0001). The clean variant gives the same pattern.
deviations: The two halves of stable1 are its first and second 15 min, as the claims file reads them; the half curves have half the data of the trial curves.
Dunnett's test is two-sided (the paper does not say); the one-sided p are shown.

outcomes.statement: Directional instability (the KLD between tuning curves) differs across trial pairs and is greater for every trial pair than between the two halves of stable1.
outcomes.source: Figure 1D, right, and its legend; Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: the change in preferred direction of directional tuning and the overall change in directional tuning (''instability'') was greater across the two stable conditions and between the stable and rotating conditions than it was between the two halves of the first stable session (Figure 1D)

statistics.about: trial pairs against the two halves of stable1
statistics.test: ANOVA, Dunnett's test against the stable1 halves

outcomes.notes: With KLD from spike counts, the three trial pairs differ (F(1.60, 182.42) = 11.74, p = 7.22e-05) and the four groups differ (F(3, 456) = 13.74, p = 1.36e-08), but Dunnett's test against the halves is significant for stable1-stable2 (p = 0.0044) and stable1-arena (p < 0.0001) and not for stable1-room (p = 0.1274; one-sided 0.0637). With KLD from rates, the ANOVAs give p = 0.000842 and 0.00256 and only stable1-arena exceeds the halves (p = 0.0008). Mean KLD (counts) 0.255, 0.218, 0.348 against 0.159 for the halves.
deviations: Dunnett's test is two-sided (the paper does not say); the one-sided p are shown.

outcomes.statement: Head direction decoded from stable1 ensemble tuning is relatively accurate in stable2 and relatively inaccurate and abruptly changing in both frames during rotation, although for some ensembles room-frame decoding is similar to stable2; seven ensembles of at least five head-direction cells were analysed.
outcomes.source: Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 2; Figure 2A and 2B
outcomes.quote: Seven ensembles of R5 cells were analyzed ... Relatively accurate decoding of the stable2 recordings (Figure 2A) contrast with relatively inaccurate and abruptly changing decoding in both the room and arena spatial frames during rotation, although for some ensembles, decoding in the room frame was similar to decoding in the stable2 condition
outcomes.notes: Seven sessions have at least five simultaneously recorded head-direction cells (four with six, three with five). With 660 ms windows the stable2 error is below the arena-frame error in 4 of 7 ensembles and below the room-frame error in 5 of 7, by the median and by the mean absolute error; 133 ms windows give the same counts. Median errors range 23.2 to 135.3 degrees in stable2, 26.7 to 103.0 in the room frame and 79.5 to 115.0 in the arena frame. In 1026R157 and 1117R157 stable2 decoding is poor (135.3 and 102.0 degrees, at or above the 5 min shifted reference; 1.4 and 0.0 degrees from it) and near chance in 1121R157 (11.7 degrees below), where the paper reports one ensemble with poor stable2 decoding. Unit 1121R157 P11C2 is left out of that session's stable2 decoding, as its stable2 file holds a different, shorter track. The count of 4 of 7 below the arena frame needs 1023R029, whose rotating tracks are shown wrong (they lag the spikes by up to 1500 samples). In the clean variant, without it, stable2 is below the arena frame in 3 of 6 ensembles and below the room frame in 4 of 6, for both measures and both windows. The outcome is decided on the files as deposited, as the paper's seven ensembles imply it used them, and depends on that session.
deviations: Assumed, as the claims file states, that "relatively accurate" means a majority, at least four of seven ensembles.
Windows without any valid direction are dropped during training; the paper's code bins them at 0 degrees (HD_Max_likelihood.py), which is taken as a defect.
Decoded directions are labelled by the start of their 10 degree bin, as in HD_Max_likelihood.py, which biases the signed error by about -5 degrees.

outcomes.statement: During rotation, frame-specific directional discharge alternated between signaling room and arena direction; four of seven ensembles showed an overall room preference and two of seven an arena preference.
outcomes.source: Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 3; Figure S2A and S2B; Figure 2C legend
outcomes.quote: 4/7 ensembles showed an overall preference to signal room directions over arena directions and 2/7 showed an overall preference to signal arena directions over room directions
outcomes.notes: Of the 16 readings the criterion names, one (45 degree bins, probabilities from the rotating trial, the SD of the ensemble's ΔIdir series, no preference when both probabilities are below 0.05) gives 4 room-preferring and 2 arena-preferring ensembles. 14 of 16 readings give more room- than arena-preferring ensembles; the others give 0 to 5 room and 0 or 1 arena ensembles. In the matching reading two ensembles are classed on probabilities near 0.05 (1117R157 room, p(ΔIdir > 2 SD) 0.0539 against p(ΔIdir < -2 SD) 0.0303; 1121R157 arena, 0.0413 against 0.0606), so the result depends on the readings. With the margin at 0.04 to 0.05 the counts are 4 and 2, at 0.055 or 0.06 3 and 2, at 0.07 3 and 1, at 0.03 5 and 2. The other arena ensemble is 1023R029, whose rotating tracks are shown wrong; in the clean variant (six ensembles) the matching reading gives 4 room and 1 arena, and no reading gives 4 and 2. The outcome is decided on the files as deposited and depends on that session.
deviations: Assumed, the readings the claims file names for the open details of Idir (direction bins, the source of the probabilities, the SD of the 2 SD rule, the margin for no preference); the paper does not fix them, and only one of 16 readings gives the reported counts.
The SD of the stable1 reading is the SD of the ensemble's summed stable1 Idir series, since ΔIdir is zero in a stable trial; the Figure 2C legend gives stable1 Idir for calibration.

outcomes.statement: The rat's relative proximity to one shock zone versus the other is anti-correlated with frame-specific directional information, so that near the room shock zone directional discharge favours the arena frame and the reverse; this holds for Idir in each frame (mean r = -0.141 ± 0.029, all p < 0.0001) and for ΔIdir (r = -0.18, p < 0.05, in the exemplar).
outcomes.source: Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraphs 3 and 4; Figure 2C and its legend; Figure S2C
outcomes.quote: This anticorrelation was observed for Idir defined for each spatial frame ... 0.141 ± 0.029; all p < 0.0001), as well as for their combination DIdir

statistics.about: Idir per frame against relative proximity, each ensemble
Idir against relative proximity, second report
ΔIdir against relative proximity, ensemble b

outcomes.notes: Under every reading the mean of the 14 frame-specific correlations is negative (-0.052 to -0.088; -0.0701 under 10 degree bins, rotating-trial probabilities and proximity reading a, the first listed) and outside both expected ranges; 11 or 12 of 14 are negative and 7 to 10 negative at p < 0.0001. The ΔIdir correlations average -0.055 to -0.128, with 5 or 6 of 7 negative; under the stable1-probability readings with 45 degree bins they average -0.126 and -0.128, within -0.132 ± 0.024. For the exemplar with the most decoded windows (1121R157) the ΔIdir r is -0.014 to -0.089. In the clean variant (six ensembles, 12 correlations) the mean is -0.049 to -0.119, within both ranges under the stable1-probability readings with 45 degree bins (-0.113, -0.119), but only 6 to 10 of 12 are negative at p < 0.0001, so the outcome is the same.
deviations: Assumed, distance to a shock zone measured to the centre point of its sector (centre angle and mid radius from the tracker header); the paper does not define relative proximity.

outcomes.statement: The frame preference ΔIdir does not vary systematically with head direction; its polar distribution over head direction in either frame is not biased toward the shock zones and does not differ from uniform.
outcomes.source: Results, Degraded Directional Tuning, paragraph 4; Figure S3 legend
outcomes.quote: did not significantly differ from uniform (average r = 0.17 ± 0.02; p > 0.17; Figure S3)
outcomes.notes: With 10 degree Idir bins and rotating-trial probabilities the average r is 0.166 (SEM 0.023), within 0.17 ± 0.02. With n the number of bins, reading (a) of the criterion, one of 14 weighted Rayleigh tests has p < 0.05 (p = 0.0134, 1121R157, room frame); with n the sum of the weights, reading (b), none does (smallest 0.346). The other Idir readings give average r 0.180 to 0.264, with 3 or 4 of 14 tests below 0.05 when n is the number of bins and 1 to 3 when n is the sum of the weights. The clean variant (12 tests) gives average r 0.154 under the main reading, with one test below 0.05 when n is the number of bins and none when n is the sum of the weights. The outcome rests on reading (a). It was reproduced in round 2 under reading (b); the second verifier found that choice unsupported, the change was proposed, and the third verifier agreed. The failing test would not survive a Bonferroni correction across the 14 tests (0.0036), but the criterion does not ask for one.
deviations: Assumed, the n of the weighted Rayleigh test is the number of bins (reading a of the criterion); the paper does not state n. Reading (a) is the one the claims file checks against the paper's p. Reading (b), the sum of the normalized weights, was first adopted as the standard n for grouped data with frequencies as weights (Zar); that reason does not hold, as the weights are rescaled mean ΔIdir, not frequencies, and their sum depends on the scaling.
Assumed, the Idir reading of 10 degree bins with probabilities from the rotating trial, the tuning curves' resolution and the trial whose information is measured.

outcomes.statement: The sub-second temporal coupling of head-direction cell pairs (Kendall correlations of spike counts at 40, 250 and 1000 ms) was maintained across stable1, rotating and stable2.
outcomes.source: Figure 3B and its legend; Results, Degraded Directional Tuning and Maintained Temporal Coupling, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: The three conditions did not differ at any of the timescales
outcomes.notes: For 146 pairs, the Fisher-transformed Kendall correlations do not differ across trials at 40 ms (F(2, 435) = 0.099, p = 0.906), 250 ms (p = 0.72) or 1000 ms (p = 0.617). The pairs' tau in stable1 correlate with the rotating trial at r = 0.959, 0.869, 0.832 and with stable2 at r = 0.965, 0.917, 0.868. The clean variant (118 pairs) gives p = 0.925, 0.738, 0.664.
deviations: 146 pairs, where the paper's degrees of freedom imply about 141.

outcomes.statement: Cell-pair discharge correlations among all 556 MEC cell pairs were preserved across trials (r² > 0.55 between the two stable trials and r² ≥ 0.52 between stable1 and rotating).
outcomes.source: Results, Degraded Directional Tuning and Maintained Temporal Coupling, paragraph 1; Figure S4
outcomes.quote: these correlations were also preserved among all the MEC cell pairs that were recorded (n = 556 pairs), regardless of the spatial functional class of the cells (r2 > 0.55 across the two stable conditions; r2 R 0.52 across the first stable and rotating session; Figure S4)
outcomes.notes: Needs the 556 pairs among the 353 MEC cells of Table S1; the dataset holds only the 115 head-direction cells (FileNameList.xlsx has 115 rows and each TSD folder 115 files).

outcomes.statement: The 115 conventionally identified head-direction cells also score high in head-direction information estimated by the Gaussian process tuning model among the 921 modelled MEC cells.
outcomes.source: Figure S5 legend
outcomes.quote: The conventionally-identified cells also scored high in head-direction information, which validates the model-based approach.
outcomes.notes: Needs the 921 MEC cells that met the model's criteria; only the 115 head-direction cells are in the dataset, so the comparison against the population cannot be made.

outcomes.statement: Cell-pair discharge correlations within the grid-tuned, position-tuned and speed-tuned subclasses of MEC cells are maintained across stable and rotating trials.
outcomes.source: Figure S6 legend
outcomes.quote: Cell-pair specific discharge correlations within subclasses of spatially-tuned cells are maintained across the stable and rotating sessions.
outcomes.notes: Depends on figs5-hd-cells-high-model-information and needs the grid, position and speed cells among the 921 modelled MEC cells, none of which are in the dataset.

outcomes.statement: The MEC head-direction cells showed no systematic tuning of firing rate to angular head velocity.
outcomes.source: Results, Transient Allocentric Registration, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: There was no systematic tuning of firing rate to angular velocity in these MEC head-direction cells (data not shown).
outcomes.notes: In 30 Hz samples of stable1, 12 of 115 cells (10.4%) correlate with signed angular velocity at p < 0.05 (binomial p = 0.0127 against 5%) and 49 of 115 (42.6%) with unsigned angular velocity (binomial p = 5.71e-33). The correlations are small (signed r -0.028 to 0.020, unsigned -0.068 to 0.040) and split in sign (6 of 12 and 26 of 49 positive). In 1 s bins 22 and 78 of 115 are significant. Successive samples are not independent, so per-cell p values are optimistic.
deviations: Assumed, as the claims file states, the measure (Pearson correlation in 30 Hz samples) and the binomial test; the paper shows no data and names no test.

outcomes.statement: Internally referenced directional tuning of head-direction cell pairs (tuning of one cell to head-direction displacement since the other's spikes) was preserved across stable1, rotating and stable2; neither its instability nor its change in preference differed between trials or from the two halves of stable1.
outcomes.source: Results, Transient Allocentric Registration, paragraph 2; Figure 4B and 4D and the legend
outcomes.quote: Internally referenced tuning to head-direction displacement was preserved across the stable and rotating conditions

statistics.about: instability, trial pairs against stable1 halves
preference change, trial pairs against stable1 halves

outcomes.notes: Main readings (5 s, cell 2 spikes before cell 1, normalization by the sum of offsets; 142 of 146 pairs with a curve in every condition). Instability differs across the three trial pairs (F(2.00, 282.00) = 9.72, p = 8.27e-05) and between trial pairs and halves (F(3, 564) = 3.11, p = 0.026); the preference change does not (p = 0.0528, p = 0.303). Mean instability 0.196 (stable1-stable2), 0.214 (room), 0.156 (arena), 0.187 (halves). In the clean variant, without the unit-trials shown wrong in the data check (114 pairs), all four tests have p ≥ 0.05 (0.0991, 0.228, 0.227, 0.744). The 30 s, after-side, occupancy and ordered-pair variants each have at least one test at p < 0.05. The gap between room (0.214) and arena (0.156) that drives the instability test comes with a shift of the displacement histograms, a median circular mean of -4.6 degrees in the room frame and 6.3 in the arena frame, against 4.0 in stable1. The displacement histograms of the tracker samples alone, with nothing of cell 2, show the same shift (-4.8, 6.9, 3.3) and the same order of KLD from stable1 (room 0.068, arena 0.048, paired p = 7.55e-08), while the valid spike counts of the two frames differ by a median of 1.4%. The samples explain the direction of the shift, not the size of the gap. The spike gap is about three times the samples-only gap, per pair the two gaps are not correlated (r = -0.01), and in the clean pairs the spike gap shrinks to 0.176 against 0.149 while the samples-only gap stays at 0.070 against 0.047. What drives the size of the gap is not established. Under the Methods' normalization by the sum of the time offsets, a single scale factor per curve, the KLD, preferred bin and strength are those of the raw displacement histogram.
deviations: One ordering per pair (cell 1 the first in file order); the paper does not say whether pairs are ordered, and the ordered pairs are a variant.

Spike and sample times are the sample times (index over rate), so that both share a clock; the paper's code mixes spike timestamps with sample times built from the header rate, which drift apart by up to about 0.8 s over a trial in these files.
For the KLD, the Krichevsky-Trofimov estimate is applied to the histogram counts (the Methods' n_i); with the occupancy normalization to the rate curve scaled to the histogram's total.

outcomes.statement: The strength of internally referenced directional tuning is similar in all conditions and frames for intervals up to 10 s, but beyond 10 s it falls in the rotating arena frame (20 to 60 s; stable1 = stable2 = rotating room > rotating arena) and at 300 to 600 s also in the rotating room frame (stable1 = stable2 > rotating room > rotating arena).
outcomes.source: Figure 4C and its legend; Results, Transient Allocentric Registration, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: during short intervals in the rotating condition, the strength of internally referenced directional tuning was similar in the two spatial frames but less so across longer intervals (Figure 4C). Specifically, internally referenced arena-frame tuning abruptly decreased after 10 s.

statistics.about: conditions at each interval up to 10 s
statistics.statistic: F(3, 564) ≤ 1.59 (printed with the glyph for ≥, read as ≤ since p > 0.19 at each interval)

statistics.about: conditions at each interval beyond 10 s
statistics.statistic: F(3, 564) ≥ 23.73 (printed with the glyph for ≤, read as ≥ since p < 10^-14 at each interval)

outcomes.notes: Main readings. The four conditions do not differ at 3, 4 and 5 s (p = 0.1747, 0.2438, 0.1703) and do at 10 s (p = 0.0106), and differ at every interval beyond 10 s (p < 0.0001). Beyond 10 s both rotating frames lose strength; the room frame falls first and is below the arena frame at 20 to 40 s (0.378 against 0.438 at 20 s), and at 20 to 60 s the two do not differ (Tukey room against arena p = 0.0611 to 0.9176), so the arena frame is not below the other three. At 300 and 600 s the room frame is below both stable trials (p ≤ 0.0002) and the arena frame below the room frame (p = 0.0135, 0.0046). The criterion's partial outcome needs the arena frame to fall below the others beyond 10 s and not before, which fails at 10 s and at 20 to 60 s, so the claim is not reproduced (changed from partially reproduced after the first verification). In the occupancy and after-side variants the arena frame is again not below all three others at every interval from 20 to 60 s, but the pattern differs. With occupancy normalization the arena frame has a lower mean than the room frame at 40 to 60 s and is below all three others at 60 s (Tukey p ≤ 0.0028); with cell 2 spikes after cell 1 the room frame is below the arena frame at 20 s (p = 0.0167). The clean variant (112 to 118 pairs) differs already at 3 to 5 s (p = 0.0109, 0.0198, 0.0127) and puts the arena frame below the room frame at p < 0.05 only from 60 s (p = 0.0368).
deviations: Strength is the Rayleigh vector length of the curve, the only reading the claims file gives.

outcomes.statement: The angular distribution of decoding error is inhomogeneous in the room frame (resultant r = 0.589) and the arena frame (r = 0.653) and differs from the distribution of sampled head directions, which is itself biased in both frames (r = 0.147 room, r = 0.378 arena).
outcomes.source: Results, Transient Allocentric Registration, paragraph 4; Figure 5A and 5B and the legend
outcomes.quote: The angular distribution of the decoded directional error was not homogeneous in the room frame (Figure 5A; resultant vector r = 0.589; Rayleigh’s test; z = 236.36; p = 0.000); nor was the error distribution similar to the head-direction distribution
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), seven ensembles pooled, 660 ms. Room-frame error r = 0.172 (n = 13381, p = 1.02e-174), arena-frame error r = 0.014 (p = 0.0626), head directions r = 0.035 (room) and 0.276 (arena), both non-uniform; Kuiper's tests p < 1e-200. In readings (b) (exemplar 1121R157) and (c) (median over ensembles) every test holds (at 660 ms, Rayleigh p from 2.17e-20 to 0.00459, Kuiper p < 1e-26), with error r 0.050 and 0.144 (b), 0.139 and 0.100 (c), and head direction r 0.293 and 0.107 (b), 0.161 and 0.339 (c). No reading puts the four r values near 0.589, 0.653, 0.147 and 0.378; one ensemble (0930R029) has a room-frame error r of 0.560. The criterion's partial outcome ("the tests hold but not every r") is met under readings (b) and (c), with no r within tolerance. The clean variant, without 1023R029, gives error r 0.177 and 0.014 pooled. Whether the claims file reads the "polar distribution of directional error" rightly is asked of a reader (questions/park-2019.yaml); under a head-direction reading, the head directions of windows decoded within 15, 30 or 45 degrees, every distribution is non-uniform (Rayleigh p ≤ 0.0036) and differs from the sampled head directions, with r 0.104 to 0.550, the highest (0.529 to 0.550) in the arena frame at 133 ms, below 0.653.
deviations: The exemplar is taken as the six-cell ensemble with the most decoded rotating windows, as four ensembles have six cells.

outcomes.statement: The room-frame decoding error histogram has strong minima at 110 and 350 degrees in the room frame, the directions of the leading edges of prominent orienting cues given the clockwise rotation; the minima correspond to the cue edges in the room frame but not in the arena frame.
outcomes.source: Results, Transient Allocentric Registration, paragraph 4; Figure 5C and 5D
outcomes.quote: Interestingly, the room frame direction decoding error distribution showed strong minima at 110 ... in the room frame, which, given the clockwise arena rotation, are the directions at which the leading edges of prominent orienting cues were located
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), mean absolute error by room head direction, with the seven ensembles pooled and 660 ms windows, the two deepest minima are at 105 and 345 degrees, within 10 of 110 and 350 (values 63.2 and 63.9 degrees in a curve from 63.2 to 91.3; the third-deepest minimum is at 325 degrees, 65.2, separated from 345 by one bin of 65.4). The two minima lie 13.8 degrees below the curve's median, against a null median of 7.5 (95th percentile 10.2, none of 1000 as deep) with each ensemble's errors circularly shifted against its head directions, and no shift puts the minima at 110 and 350. The clean variant (six ensembles) puts them at 115 and 345. Reading (b), the signed error histogram, puts them at 75 and 115 degrees; the exemplar and the 133 ms windows put them elsewhere (for example 235 and 335 degrees for reading a at 133 ms), so the match holds under one reading and window only. The cue positions are not tested.

findings.statement: The dataset holds only the 115 head-direction cells. The other MEC cells of Table S1 (353 cells, 556 pairs), the 921 cells of the Gaussian process model, the LFP, the waveforms and the pretraining and training sessions are not in it, so the findings of Figures 1A, 1C (LFP), S4, S5 and S6 cannot be tested.

FileNameList.xlsx misaligns its stable2 column for five units of session 1121R157. The rows for SA1 P11C2, P11C3, P11C4, P9C2 and P9C3 list SA2 P11C3, P11C4, P9C2, P9C3 and cl1.P11C2, one row off. Its second sheet also names the stable2 files of 1020R035 and 1030R035 as CON files, while the files are named SA2.

The rotating-trial spike file of unit 1024R157 P9C1 (RA_rm and RA_ar) holds exactly its stable1 spike times (2919 spikes, same timestamps), while the other units of the session have distinct rotating spikes, so one of the two files holds the wrong spikes.

The rotating room-frame track of session 1211R039 (RA_rm) is identical to that of session 1212R039, and does not agree with its own arena-frame track (the distance from the arena centre differs by a median of 22 px, against 0.3 px in other sessions). Its two .dat files agree with each other (0.31 px), its arena-frame TSD track agrees with its arena .dat file (0.49 px), and its room-frame TSD track agrees with the room .dat file of 1212R039 (0.32 px) and not with its own (22.1 px), so its room-frame TSD files carry another session's track.

In sessions 1009R029, 1015R029, 1023R029 and 1025R029 the room-frame and arena-frame tracks of the rotating trial disagree with each other (median 6.9 to 13.5 px in distance from the arena centre at the best constant lag) and with the session's .dat files, which agree with each other (0.31 px). The lag of the TSD tracks behind the .dat track grows through the trial, to about 700 to 1500 samples in the room frame and half that in the arena frame, so the spikes cannot be aligned with both frames. Excluding these sessions changes the room-frame results of the paper's directionality and internally referenced tuning comparisons.

The stable2 file of unit 1017R035 P11C2 states a sampling interval of 2000 samples/s and a first timestamp of 5, against about 30.02 samples/s in every other file; its 54185 samples and 2123 spike times span 28.5 min, and 614 of its spikes lie more than 3 samples off the line that relates spike times to the samples that hold them.
The stable2 file of unit 1121R157 P11C2 (named cl1) holds 26954 samples, half the trial, with a track that differs from the other units of the session.

The spike timestamps run ahead of the tracker samples by about 0.05% (about 25 samples, 0.8 s, by the end of a 30 min trial) when sample times are computed from the header's sampling rate and first timestamp; the data descriptor does not say how spike times relate to samples.

Per rat, the dataset's head-direction cells match Table S1 except R029 (40 against 41) and R523 (2 against 1), and the 44 sessions give 146 simultaneously recorded head-direction pairs, against 142 in the Results.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper's full text. The verifier checked the member list of data.zip (its central directory, filelist.txt and checksums.md5) for the blocked claims, and tested the helpers on synthetic data (rm_anova against statsmodels AnovaRM and the Greenhouse-Geisser formula, rayleigh_p, kuiper_two, tukey_rm, internal_tuning against a brute-force loop, kld, and decode). It had no attempt record and took the claims from the claims file.

disagreements.reason: The ANOVA is significant at 10 s (p = 0.011). Under no variant is the arena frame below the room frame at 20 to 60 s; the room frame falls instead (at 20 to 40 s it is below the arena frame). [Amended by the verifier in round 2. This sentence is wrong. At 60 s the occupancy variant (p = 0.0028) and the clean variant (p = 0.0368) both put the arena frame below the room frame. The outcome does not change, because the ANOVA is already significant at 10 s.] The pairs from the four R029 sessions with warped rotating tracks enter the analysis, which has no clean variant.

Error r is 0.17 (room) and 0.014 (arena, p = 0.06) pooled, against 0.589 and 0.653, and no reading or window comes within tolerance. The claims file may misread the paper; the paper compares the "polar distribution of directional error" with the sampled head-direction distribution by Kuiper's test, and Figure 5C places its minima "in the room frame", which suggests a distribution over head direction, not the Rayleigh test on signed error angles. No such reading was run, and the analysis has no clean variant.

verifications.reviewed: The full executed notebook of the first revision, with its conclusion cells and summary, the helper module, the claims file, the attempt record and the entry README, with the paper's full text. It took the counts of claims and outcomes from the attempt record (22 claims, 9 reproduced, 5 partially reproduced, 3 not reproduced, 5 blocked, six marked assumed). It also reported two points that bear on no claim. The data check (cell 8) and the record's findings stated numbers no output printed (median 7 to 13 px at the best constant lag, the .dat files of 1211R039 agreeing and its arena-frame TSD track matching its arena .dat file exactly, 2919 spikes for 1024R157 P9C1, 614 spikes far from their sample for 1017R035 P11C2); and the README said the notebook takes about two minutes where it printed 2.9. In reply a data-check cell now prints each of these numbers. It gives 6.9 to 13.5 px, and it shows the arena-frame track of 1211R039 agrees with its .dat file (0.49 px, against 0.23 and 0.36 px in 1022R029) but does not match it exactly, so the text and findings now give these values. The README now says about three minutes.

paper_notes.statement: Questions for the authors on momentary directional information (Figures 2C, S2, S3), which this attempt could not settle from the paper. Which direction bins and which trial's probabilities define p(n|d) and p(n) in Idir; which SD the 2 SD rule uses, given that the exemplar's p(ΔIdir > 2 SD) = 0.56 exceeds what the SD of the ΔIdir series itself allows; what margin defines no frame preference; how relative proximity to the two shock zones is computed; and the n of the weighted Rayleigh test of Figure S3. The 16 readings tested give 0 to 5 room-preferring ensembles, and only one gives the reported 4 and 2.

Questions for the authors on the statistics and on internally referenced tuning. Whether the Tukey-Kramer tests after the repeated-measures ANOVAs use the repeated-measures error term (the outcome for Figure 1C directionality depends on it); how speed is computed for Figure 1C; whether internally referenced tuning uses ordered pairs, which pairs were dropped (the degrees of freedom imply about 130 to 137 of 142), and what "divided by the sum of the time offsets" means, since dividing a histogram by one number does not change its shape.

The decoding window is 660 ms in the STAR Methods (20 samples in the code, 667 ms at 30 Hz) and 133 ms in the Figure 2 legend. The arena-frame error z is 289.63 in the Results and 153.24 and 230.58 in the Figure 5 legend, the values given for the head-direction distributions.

entries.name: park-2019
entries.title: MEC head-direction cells on a rotating arena (Park et al. 2019)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Park, Keeley, Savin, Ranck and Fenton (2019) on CRCNS hc-20, which holds the spike trains of 115 medial entorhinal head-direction cells from 13 rats, recorded in stable, rotating and stable trials of a place avoidance task, with the tracker files of those trials. It compares directional tuning, firing rates, pair correlations, ensemble decoding, momentary directional information and internally referenced tuning across trials and frames. The other MEC cells, the LFP and the training sessions are not in the data set.
